## Within-gene driver breakdown for the top combined genes

For the top 10 combined-layer genes per ancestry, the per-phenotype lead
associations across all modalities (ungrouped layer):

```{r driver-breakdown}
top10 <- top_combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  select(ancestry, gene_id, gene_symbol, driver_modality)
breakdown <- top10 %>%
  inner_join(ungrouped %>% select(ancestry, gene_id, modality, phenotype_id,
                                  variant_id, af, slope, pval_beta, qval),
             by = c("ancestry", "gene_id")) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, gene_id) %>% arrange(pval_beta, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id)) %>%
  select(ancestry, gene_id, gene_symbol, modality, phenotype_id, variant_id,
         af, slope, pval_beta, qval)
write_tsv(breakdown, file.path(params$table_dir, "driver_breakdown_top10.tsv"))
knitr::kable(breakdown %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>%
               select(-ancestry) %>% head(20), digits = 3,
             caption = "EAS top-10 genes: top 5 phenotypes each (ungrouped layer).")
```

# Biological interpretation

```{r interp-numbers}
mod_leader <- if (nrow(n_eg_mod) > 0) {
  n_eg_mod %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(total = sum(n)) %>%
    slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
} else NULL
enrich_highlight <- if (exists("enrich_results") && length(enrich_results) > 0) {
  bind_rows(enrich_results) %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
    slice_min(p_value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
    summarise(hl = paste(sprintf("%s — %s (%s, g:SCS p = %s)", query_set,
                                 term_name, source, signif(p_value, 2)),
                         collapse = "; ")) %>% pull(hl)
} else NA_character_
```

**The discovery landscape: `r n_fdr05` FDR ≤ 5% associations —
`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS and `r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes in the primary
combined-layer catalog** (n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`/`r n_samp["EUR"]`, MAF ≥
0.01 + MAC ≥ 5, genome-wide permutation calibration). Strongest per
ancestry:
`r paste(sprintf("%s: %s", top_by_anc$ancestry, apply(top_by_anc, 1, function(r) sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s, r² ≈ %.2f)", symd(r[["gene_id"]]), r[["modality"]], r[["layer"]], signif(as.numeric(r[["qval"]]), 2), approx_r2(as.numeric(r[["slope"]]), as.numeric(r[["af"]]))))), collapse = "; ")`.
`r if (!is.null(hit_r2)) sprintf("Hit effect sizes (r² %.2f–%.2f) sit in the class the power floor permits.", hit_r2[1], hit_r2[2])`
All hits should be treated as candidates: visual QC of phenotype levels by
genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts come before functional
claims.

Three **characterization** observations:

1. **Modality composition.** `r if (!is.null(mod_leader)) paste(sprintf("%s leads the %s grouped-eGene breakdown (%d of %d)", mod_leader$modality, mod_leader$ancestry, mod_leader$n, mod_leader$total), collapse = "; ") else "No grouped-layer eGenes."`
   PANTRY's central finding was that non-expression modalities carry the
   largest share of regulatory signal; the driver-modality composition of
   the catalog (above) tests whether that ordering holds in placenta.
2. **Ancestry sharing.** `r if (!is.null(fisher_overlap)) sprintf("%d of %d EAS and %d EUR combined-layer eGenes are shared (Fisher OR %.2f, p = %s vs the tested-in-both universe).", length(shared_eg), length(eg_eas), length(eg_eur), fisher_overlap$estimate, signif(fisher_overlap$p.value, 2)) else "Ancestry overlap was not computed (empty eGene set)."`
   Shared eGenes are the cross-ancestry replication signal; specific sets
   are candidates for ancestry-biased regulation.
3. **Functional enrichment.** `r if (!is.na(enrich_highlight)) paste0("Top g:Profiler term per set: ", enrich_highlight, ". Full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv.") else "No significant enrichment terms (or sets too small for ORA) — see the enrichment section."`

## Literature context

**Positive control: the ERAP1/ERAP2 locus (5q15).** The strongest signal
shared across ancestries is *ERAP2* — a top-10 combined-layer gene in both
strata (EAS #6, q = 1.1×10⁻¹⁹, expression driver; EUR #4,
q = 7.2×10⁻²⁹, **isoform-expression** driver) — with *ERAP1* the #1 gene
in EUR (q = 3.3×10⁻³¹, alt_polyA driver). *ERAP2* is a canonical preeclampsia risk
locus: fetal-genome variants at *ERAP2* associate with preeclampsia in
Australian/Norwegian ([Johnson et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00439-009-0714-x)),
Brazilian ([Ferreira et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-86240-z)),
and African American ([Hill et al. 2011](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2350-12-64))
cohorts, and ERAP1/ERAP2 are differentially expressed in preeclamptic
placentas ([Seamon et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2020.00396)).
The EUR driver being isoform expression is mechanism-consistent: the
preeclampsia-associated *ERAP2* variation tags a haplotype under balancing
selection whose molecular effect is alternative splicing and
nonsense-mediated decay of *ERAP2* transcripts
([Andrés et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1001157);
[Raja & Kuiper 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41435-023-00225-8);
[Ye et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.240390.118)) — exactly the
phenotype class our isoform-expression layer measures. Recovering this
locus, through the expected modality, is direct evidence that the atlas
captures disease-relevant placental regulation.

**Top combined-layer genes, per ancestry.** EAS: the top signal is an
uncharacterized lncRNA (*ENSG00000290199*, q = 3.7×10⁻²³) — a novel
candidate with no annotation; *PGM1* (#2, expression driver) — placental
phosphoglucomutase activity is long established
([Fazi et al. 1990](https://doi.org/10.1080/00327489008050198)) and PGM1
loss disrupts cellular energy homeostasis
([Conte et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms24098247)), relevant to
placental glycogen handling in diabetic pregnancy
([Lafta et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.28969/ijeir.v10.i2.r3)); *FBLN1*
(#3, isoform-expression driver) — fibulin-1 functions in placentation
([Singh et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.placenta.2005.10.009)),
placental ECM remodeling in late-onset preeclampsia
([García-Montero et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.3390/medsci14030364)),
and maternal plasma fibulin-1 tracking pregnancy progression
([Orvik et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12884-021-04110-y)); *IQCG*
(#4, expression driver) — ciliary/flagellar function with no prior
placental association (novel candidate); *PSCA* (#5, alt_polyA driver) —
overexpressed in gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
([Feng et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2559.2007.02925.x));
*RPS28* (#7, expression driver) — small-subunit ribosomal protein with no
prior placental association (novel candidate); *TOR1AIP1* (#8,
isoform-expression driver) — the LAP1 nuclear-envelope protein; biallelic
loss causes multisystemic nuclear envelopathy with growth retardation
([Fichtman et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08493-7);
reviewed in [Mackels et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms24086911)),
with no prior placental association; *SPSB2* (#9, expression driver) — an
E3-ligase adaptor targeting iNOS for proteasomal degradation
([Kuang et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.200912087);
[Li et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.niox.2021.04.004)), placing it
in nitric-oxide biology central to placental vascular function; *MRPL43*
(#10, intron-retention driver) — a mitoribosomal protein already known to
carry an antagonistic cis-eQTL acting oppositely on transcription and
translation
([Han & Lee 2022](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12863-022-01057-7)), and fellow
mitoribosomal subunit *MRPL13* drives trophoblast mitochondrial stress in
early-onset preeclampsia
([Chen et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/reprod/xaag016)); *ELP5* (#11,
alt_polyA driver) — an Elongator-complex subunit required for tRNA
wobble-uridine modification
([Huang et al. 2005](https://doi.org/10.1261/rna.7247705)), no prior
placental association; *THNSL2* (#12, expression driver) — no prior
placental association (novel candidate). EUR: *ERAP1* (#1) and *ERAP2*
(#4) above; *ZSCAN9* (#2, expression driver) — KRAB zinc-finger with no
prior placental association (novel candidate); *CTNND1* (#3, RNA-editing
driver) — p120-catenin is required for trophoblast proliferation and
lineage specification at implantation
([Qin et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1093/biolre/ioae163)) and sits in the
Wnt-regulated invasion program
([Knöfler & Pollheimer 2013](https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2013.00190));
*CTSB* (#5, RNA-editing driver) — cathepsin B, whose serum level is
elevated in preeclampsia and tracks disease severity
([Kim et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-016-4129-3);
[Park et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-020-05478-6)); *STBD1*
(#6, expression driver) — the glycophagy receptor linking glycogen to
selective autophagy
([Zhang et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2402817121);
[Tang et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcp.31078)), a second
glycogen-metabolism hit alongside *PGM1*; *APIP* (#7, stability driver) —
an anti-apoptotic Apaf-1 inhibitor protective under hypoxia/ischemia
([Cho et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.m405747200)) that is also
the methionine-salvage enzyme mtnB
([Mary et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0052877)) — a
plausible hypoxia-response link to placental biology; *WDR91* (#8,
expression driver) — a Rab7 effector in endolysosomal trafficking
([Rapiteanu et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1111/tra.12409);
[Ma et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.str.2024.09.023)), no prior
placental association; *MEAK7* (#9, expression driver) — an
mTORC1-associated protein; trophoblast mTOR signaling controls placental
nutrient transport and fetal growth
([Shao et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2017092118);
[Rosario et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1042/cs20243293)); *ARFGAP3*
(#10, isoform-expression driver) — COPI vesicle-coat assembly at the Golgi
([Kartberg et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.m110.180380)), no
prior placental association; *GBP3* (#11, isoform-expression driver) — an
interferon-inducible GTPase in cell-autonomous immunity
([Tretina et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20182031);
[Kirkby et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibs.2023.07.002)), no
prior placental association; *KANSL1-AS1* (#12, expression driver) —
placental expression of this lncRNA tracks infant birthweight in the GAPPS
cohort
([Hussey et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1017/s204017442500011x)).

**Modality-matched covariates, in line with QTL practice.** Latent-factor
covariates are a standard power lever in QTL mapping
([Stegle et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2011.457)), and
splicing layers — quantified annotation-free from intron usage
([Li et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-017-0004-9)) — have
hidden structure that need not track gene expression. The per-modality HCP
choice behaved as that practice predicts: EUR splicing was null under
expression-derived factors and recovers
`r n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"]`
eGenes at its own k\* = 5, while the EAS splicing null is flat across the
entire k grid, excluding covariate specification as its cause.

Sub-threshold top-ranked genes (tables above) remain prioritization hints
only`r if (any(mac_tab$n_lt5 > 0)) " — and the flagged low-carrier rows should be discounted outright" else ""`.

# Limitations and next steps

1. **Power.** n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`/`r n_samp["EUR"]` with a ~12k-gene
   testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects.
   Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY's
   n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and
   the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
2. **EAS splicing is near-null.** The layer yields a handful of FDR ≤ 5%
   eGenes while EUR splicing — at a higher detection floor — yields
   `r n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"]`.
   The EAS result is robust to HCP count (flat k-grid), so covariate
   specification is excluded as the cause; the leading candidate is
   cross-cohort heterogeneity in junction-level quantification (EAS pools
   four cohorts spanning single- and paired-end protocols). Revisiting
   splicing quantification harmonization across the EAS cohorts, and adding
   EAS cohorts, are the targeted next steps.
3. **Technical replicates.** 25 mapped individuals (4 EAS, 21 EUR) have two
   RNA-seq runs. Phenotype values come from the single ComBat-processed run
   per individual, while run-level covariates (cell-type fractions, QC
   metrics) are averaged across the pair — a slight phenotype/covariate
   misalignment for those individuals. Future runs will collapse replicates
   at the count level before batch correction so phenotypes and covariates
   are averaged consistently, with a pre-collapse replicate-concordance QC
   gate.
4. **Carrier-count propagation.** `r if (all(mac_tab$n_lt5 == 0)) "The MAC ≥ 5 floor propagated cleanly to every mapping output (audit table above)." else "The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so low-carrier tests persist in some mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source."`
5. **Ancestry asymmetry.** EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every
   modality (ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are
   restricted to genes tested in both.
6. **No pooled cross-ancestry inference** was performed. If combined
   discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope
   meta-analysis are the clean options.
7. **Stepwise secondary signals**: `r if (n_secondary == 0) "none called in any layer." else sprintf("%d groups carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (table above).", n_secondary)`
8. **Fine-mapping and colocalization are out of scope.** The
   natural follow-ups on the FDR-significant catalog are SuSiE fine-mapping
   per eGene locus, GWAS colocalization (coloc/eCAVIAR) against placental
   and pregnancy-outcome GWAS, and locus-zoom visual QC of each hit
   (nominal-scan extraction + LD from the ancestry-matched genotype panel).
9. **Replication path**: the FDR-significant hits are the priorities for
   lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC
   of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for each.

# Reproducibility

- Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined / stepwise),
  MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, **Storey
  q-values** on pval_beta via the R `qvalue` package (singularity-R bridge).
  Covariates: as described (first-5 PCs + HCP_1–k\* + sex/GA/cell types;
  maternal fraction excluded before correlation pruning; no cap). Genotype
  PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
- Pipeline scripts: this repository (`05_qtl_mapping/`, scripts 19–30 +
  `compute_qvalues.R`; genotype pooling in `01_genotype_imputation/`).
- Report code: `report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd` + `xqtl_report_functions.R`;
  figures in `figures/`, tables in `tables/`.
- Gene symbols: `gene_map.tsv` regenerated in full from the normalized GTF
  (config `normalized_gtf`) by `make_report_archive.sh` at archive time —
  covers every tested gene, version-stripped IDs.
